facts.fact: UNHCR reports it had registered a cumulative 79,019 refugees and asylum-seekers in Libya by the end of 2024, 36,159 of them new in 2024, at its Tripoli registration centre, with documentation (a UNHCR refugee certificate) issued to them.
facts.system: UNHCR registration, Sarraj Registration Centre, Tripoli (proGres)

facts.fact: UNHCR reports East-based Libyan authorities register medically cleared Sudanese new arrivals in Alkufra and issue them a Registration Security Card, which UNHCR says is not recognized in the West.
UNHCR reports 100% of IDPs in Libya held legally recognized identity documents in 2024, and 31.35% of refugees and asylum-seekers did.

UNHCR reports that from January 2024 its Tripoli registration team used the Libya Appointment and Services System (LASS) to schedule and process registration cases, and that authorities in the West were reluctant to carry out registration themselves.
